title: Grand Theft Auto V Enhanced
provenance: tested locally on Apple Silicon (M1 Pro, macOS 26.6.2, engine x64-crossover26.3-r4) on 2026-09-08: it launches and loads under vkd3d and the GPU device is then lost, twice, at default and at minimum settings
notes: Starts under vkd3d, refuses under D3DMetal, and neither finishes. The game needs Highball's Wine 11 engine (CrossOver 26.3 base) and two graphics modes in one process tree: the Rockstar Games Launcher signs in under DXMT, the game is DirectX 12 only. Under D3DMetal it quits at once with ERR_GFX_D3D_NOD3D12, and what causes that is NOT yet known: the game creates a D3D12 device, makes 137 capability queries that all succeed, creates a DXGI factory and enumerates an adapter, and then refuses. Under vkd3d it reaches the story-mode loading screen at 53-62 fps and then loses the GPU device because MoltenVK cannot translate some of its shaders to Metal. Turn BattlEye off in the launcher first (Settings > My installed games), its driver cannot load under Wine. GTA Online is out of reach regardless. If sign-in is refused with #1.000.7, set the Mac's clock (see the rockstar recipe).

requiresLauncher.name: Rockstar Games Launcher
requiresLauncher.note: Required for sign-in. Works on the Wine 11 engine under DXMT with the cross-process browser fix; sign-in verified 2026-09-08 once the Mac's clock was right. The game must then run under vkd3d while the launcher stays on DXMT.

anticheat.note: GTA Online only; BattlEye's Linux/Proton support does not extend to macOS.

knownIssues.symptom: ERR_GFX_D3D_NOD3D12 within seconds of starting, under the D3DMetal graphics mode
knownIssues.cause: cause not established on Apple M1 Pro hardware, and a long list of candidates has been excluded by measurement on 2026-09-08 (macOS 26.6.2, engine x64-crossover26.3-r4, D3DMetal 3.0 and Apple's D3DMetal 4.0b2 from Game Porting Toolkit 4). Excluded: the DirectX 12 Agility SDK loader (the game declares SDK 611 and never calls D3D12GetInterface; supplying it changed nothing); device creation (succeeds at 12_0 on the real adapter); capability values (137 CheckFeatureSupport calls all return S_OK, and forcing every one of them to report supported changes nothing); the advertised feature level (D3DMetal claims 12_2 and even accepts device creation there, but making it report and behave exactly like vkd3d, 12_0 with E_INVALIDARG above, changes nothing); ray tracing (D3DM_SUPPORT_DXR=1 raises the tier to 1.1, no change); the GPU identity presented (vendor, device and description overridden, no change); DXGI (factory, adapter enumeration, GetDesc3, outputs, tearing, video memory budget and swapchain creation in seven configurations all succeed, identically to vkd3d); Highball's own timestamp shim (removing it entirely changes nothing); and Metal 4 mode. The game creates a device, reads capabilities, creates no resource, raises no exception, and quits. Field reports are consistent with a hardware floor: it is reported working on M4 Pro and M5 Pro and never on M1 or M2, and it uses hardware ray tracing, which Apple GPUs only have from M3 onward (this Mac reports GPU family Apple 7). That is a correlation, not a proof, and it does not explain why the same Mac starts the game under vkd3d.
knownIssues.fix: none known. Not an app-level problem.

knownIssues.symptom: Under vkd3d it loads to a black screen with only the progress bar, then exits on its own near the end of the load
knownIssues.cause: MoltenVK cannot translate two classes of the game's shaders to Metal, and one of them is a deliberate upstream limitation rather than a bug. Measured 2026-09-08 on an M1 Pro, macOS 26.6.2, engine x64-crossover26.3-r4 with MoltenVK 1.4.1: 42 graphics pipelines fail with 'Component decoration is not supported in tessellation shaders' (84 occurrences, control and evaluation stages), and 27 compute pipelines fail with MSL compile errors on vkd3d's bindless descriptor arrays ('reinterpret_cast casts away qualifiers', 'indirection requires pointer operand'). The tessellation one is an explicit SPIRV_CROSS_THROW in SPIRV-Cross's spirv_msl.cpp, with the comment 'Technically tessellation as well, but it is too complicated to support', still present on main, so a newer MoltenVK does not fix it. Setting the game's Tessellation option to 0 cuts the graphics failures from 42 to 13 and avoids the device loss, but does not eliminate them: the game still builds tessellation pipelines for some passes. Stock MoltenVK cannot be substituted to test newer translation code, because the engine needs an x86_64 build carrying the MVK_SHADOW_IMPORT patch that lets it work behind Wine's winevulkan; upstream fat builds report no Vulkan 1.3 device and nothing starts.
knownIssues.fix: none at the app level. The tessellation half needs SPIRV-Cross to implement Component decoration for tessellation, which upstream has declined as too complicated. Turning the game's Tessellation setting to 0 reduces the failures and removes the device loss, but the run still does not complete.
